Subject: Question on advance billing allocation + VAT for order form

Rafael —

Thanks for sending the order form draft last week. A couple of quick things our finance team flagged before we run this through procurement:

- The schedule shows a single upfront advance invoice for 12 months. Can we split that into an advance + quarterly reconciliations so our treasury team can manage cashflow?
- For VAT: Atelier is registered in Ireland; our AP team expects Redwood to issue invoices with VAT charged to our entity, but they also asked whether Redwood will accept gross-up or whether we should apply reverse charge.
- Is there an escrow or credit-hold option for the upfront so we don’t lose runway if there are onboarding delays?

If you can point me to the recommended flow (invoice recipient + any evidence we need to provide), we’ll escalate internally.

Best,

Ava — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below, then I’ll pull in legal for the final tax language.

1) Advance split: We can split the upfront into an initial deposit (60%) + three quarterly invoices for the remainder (scheduled month 4/8/12). I’ve attached a sample payment schedule. That keeps most of the cashflow on your side but limits runway exposure for you.

2) VAT handling: For EU customers we typically either: (a) charge VAT to the billed entity (if Redwood is registered in the customer country), or (b) invoice net and the customer applies reverse charge. For Atelier (Ireland) I think reverse charge is the cleaner path — you’d self-account for VAT. However, if you need Redwood to charge VAT, we’ll need your VAT registration number and possibly a place-of-supply confirmation.

3) Escrow / credit-hold: We don’t usually do bank escrow, but we can accept a dedicated escrow account (third-party) or create a staged-credit holdback on the invoice (e.g., 10% retained until onboarding milestone M1). If you’d like escrow wording, we’ll need procurement to confirm the escrow agent and timeline.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm payment milestone language and whether sales ops can add a staged-credit row on the order form?

Ava — I’ll loop Legal (Kimberly) to redline the VAT clause and the holdback language.

Thanks,
Rafael

Team / Ava — forwarding our legal read. See the short redline summary below and attached PDF with inline changes. 

Summary (high level):
- VAT: Recommend reverse charge be default for EU customers where customer is VAT-registered. This avoids Redwood needing to register in Ireland and keeps tax administration with the customer. We will add a data field on the order form to capture Customer VAT number; failure to provide it within 30 days will default to charging VAT and customer will remain liable for any retrospective tax.
- Advance / holdback: We can accept a 60% initial non-refundable deposit, with a 10% onboarding holdback refundable upon completion of Milestone M1 (onboarding sign-off). The remainder is invoiced quarterly. We explicitly disallow escrow arrangements that transfer custody of license keys or access (security risk). If escrow is mandatory, procurement must supply the escrow agent contract for legal review and Redwood reserves the right to decline.
- Net terms: Default Net 30 for recurring invoices; upfront deposit due on receipt. If customer requires Net 45, Sales must approve credit and optionally require a credit check / PO.

I attached OrderForm_Tax_Appendix_Redline.pdf showing the concrete language. Ben, update the order form lines for: deposit %, holdback %, payment dates, and VAT field. Rafael, please confirm if this is acceptable to the customer or whether they need Redwood to charge VAT.

Thanks,
